items.title: US to Sell F-35s to Saudi Arabia in $24.3 Billion Deal
items.summary:
The State Department notified Congress that it plans to sell Saudi Arabia up to 48 F-35 warplanes in a first-time sale that could be worth as much as $24.3 billion. The sale of the Lockheed Martin Corp. fighter jet to Saudi Arabia has been in the works for a number of years. President Donald Trump signaled in November the US would sell F-35s to the Kingdom, offering Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman a prize he’s long cherished, ahead of a visit to the White House that month. Meantime, the Pentagon and Lockheed Martin Corp. are moving to speed up the production of a new classified air-to-air missile for US Air Force and Navy jets that’s seen as vital to deterring China.

For more, we speak with Wayne Sanders, Senior Defense Research Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Juventus hammer Njimigen 5-0 as keeper suffers Europa League nightmare
items.author: Philip O'connor
items.creator: Philip O'connor
items.summary: Juventus hammered Dutch side NEC Nijmegen 5-0 at home with help from two errors by goalkeeper Nikolas Polster and Olympique de Marseille of France lost 4-1 away to Besiktas as the first round of Europa League matches wrapped up on Thursday.
items.body:
Juventus hammered Dutch side NEC Nijmegen 5-0 at home with help from two errors by goalkeeper Nikolas Polster and Olympique de Marseille of France lost 4-1 away to Besiktas as the first round of Europa League matches wrapped up on Thursday.
The first howler from Nijmegen 's Polster allowed Nicolas Gonzalez to nip in ahead of him and steal the ball to give Juve the lead in the ninth minute. A goal from Kerim Alajbegovic and a penalty from Nick Woltemade sent them in 3-0 up at the break.
Zeki Celik made it 4-0 in the 75th minute before Polster again came out of his goal and failed to clear the ball, and this time it was Randal Kolo Muani who rolled it into the empty net to complete the rout.
Marseille's disastrous start to the season continued as they followed up three straight defeats in Ligue 1 with a comprehensive beating at the hands of Besiktas, with the Turkish side scoring three goals without reply in the second half en route to victory.
Scottish champions Celtic also suffered an embarrassing defeat as Ferencvaros of Hungary coasted to an easy 3-1 away win, while in London Crystal Palace scored three times in the first half as the Premier League side cruised to a 3-0 win over Lech Poznan of Poland.
Fellow English side Bournemouth grabbed a 2-1 win away to Real Sociedad in Spain, while Norwegian side Lillestrom fell to a 2-1 loss at home in their first game in the competition's group stage to Portugal's Torreense, who had Nuha Jatta sent off for picking up a second yellow card late on.
Earlier in the evening, Greek side OFI Crete beat Germany's Hoffenheim 2-0 at home, while RB Salzburg picked up a 1-0 win away to Levski Sofia in Bulgaria.

items.title: No hay evidencia de propuesta atribuida a Sheinbaum para impedir que mayores de 40 años conduzcan
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: No hay registro de que la presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, haya impulsado una iniciativa para prohibir que las personas mayores de 40 años “utilicen celulares y manejen” en el país.
items.body:
No hay registro de que la presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, haya impulsado una iniciativa para prohibir que las personas mayores de 40 años “utilicen celulares y manejen” en el país.
Publicaciones en TikTok, Instagram y Facebook comparten la propuesta atribuida a Sheinbaum en la que dice: “En México vamos a prohibir que los viejitos de 40 años en adelante utilicen celulares y manejen. Debemos evitar accidentes. Ya esas personas adultas deben quedarse en su casa y no salir a la vía pública”.
El equipo de la Coordinación General de Comunicación Social y Vocería del Gobierno de la República dijo que es falso en un mensaje en WhatsApp del 3 de septiembre de 2026.
No se hallaron registros de una iniciativa similar del poder ejecutivo en el sitio web del Sistema de Información Legislativa, ni menciones en 2026 en las gacetas del Senado y de la Cámara de Diputados .
Al 16 de septiembre, tampoco se hallaron reportes creíbles de medios sobre la iniciativa atribuida a Sheinbaum y una búsqueda en las cuentas de redes sociales de la presidenta no arrojó resultados relacionados.
La Ley General de Movilidad y Seguridad Vial de México, en el artículo 49 fracción décima, sí recoge la prohibición para conductores de hablar por teléfono celular o enviar mensajes en dispositivos electrónicos, salvo que se realice con tecnología de manos libres, pero no se hallaron menciones sobre una restricción etaria para mayores de 40 años.
VEREDICTO Sin evidencia. No hay registro de una iniciativa atribuida a la presidenta mexicana Claudia Sheinbaum sobre prohibir que las personas mayores de 40 años “utilicen celulares y manejen” en el país. El equipo de la Coordinación General de Comunicación Social y Vocería del Gobierno de la República dijo que es falso.
Reuters Fact Check ofrece información confiable mediante su canal de WhatsApp para México . Envíenos un mensaje con el contenido en español que desea que verifiquemos.
Este artículo fue realizado por el equipo de Reuters Fact Check. Lea más sobre nuestro trabajo de verificación de afirmaciones en las redes sociales.

items.title: US FCC approves foreign investment in Paramount Warner merger deal
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Federal Communications Commission on Thursday said it approved a Paramount Skydance request for foreign investments backing its acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery despite a group of senators raising concerns.
items.body:
The Federal Communications Commission on Thursday said it approved a Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) request for foreign investments backing its acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) despite a group of senators raising concerns.
In a decision released by the FCC's media bureau, the commission placed limits on the extent of foreign investment in the deal and said foreign investors can have no voting stock and "will not have any influence, direction, or control over or provide any commentary or guidance on Paramount’s content decisions, company management," or access to non-public data on U.S. citizens.

items.title: US Senate confirms former Thomas law clerk to serve as judge in Texas
items.author: Nate Raymond
items.creator: Nate Raymond
items.summary: A corporate litigator who clerked for US Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas won Senate confirmation on Thursday to serve as a federal judge in a Texas court that has become a favorite for conservative litigants challenging Democratic policies.
items.body:
A corporate litigator who clerked for US Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas won Senate confirmation on Thursday to serve as a federal judge in a Texas court that has become a favorite for conservative litigants challenging Democratic policies.
The Republican-led Senate voted 49-45 in favor of Dallas-based Kirkland & Ellis partner Kasdin Mitchell becoming a life-tenured judge in the US District Court for the Northern District of Texas.
The vote gave President Donald Trump his 55th confirmed judicial appointment of his second term, as the White House looks to [USN:L1N4500N3 TEXT:"fill as many court vacancies"] as possible before the year's end amid the looming risk that Democrats retake the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections.
Those 55 add to 234 previous appointments Trump made in his first term to the lower courts and the US Supreme Court, helping shift the judiciary's ideological balance to the right.
Mitchell will join a Texas court that is [USN:L1N3L50JD TEXT:"dominated by other Republican-appointed judges"], which made it a popular forum for conservative litigants and business groups challenging Democratic President Joe Biden's agenda during his term.
Of the court's 10 active judges, only one was appointed by a Democrat and seven were named by Trump, including Mitchell.
A Federalist Society member in her early 40s, Mitchell served as assistant press secretary to First Lady Laura Bush before attending Yale Law School and became an appellate lawyer in the Alabama attorney general's office after graduating.
She went on to clerk for now-Chief US Circuit Judge William Pryor of the 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals before later clerking from 2016 to 2017 for Thomas, the senior member of the Supreme Court's 6-3 conservative majority.
She joined Kirkland & Ellis in 2017, where she has represented companies ranging from Meta Platforms to 3M. According to her financial disclosure report, she earned nearly $3.48 million as a partner at the firm last year.
While at Kirkland, she worked alongside now-former partner Paul Clement as counsel to the New York State Rifle & Pistol Association in a landmark US Supreme Court case that reshaped modern firearms regulation.
The Supreme Court in that 2022 case, [USN:L1N2YG2O9 TEXT:"New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen"], declared for the first time that the US Constitution protects an individual's right to carry a handgun in public for self-defense.
It also established a new test for assessing firearms laws, saying restrictions must be "consistent with this nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation."
Last year, the Supreme Court appointed Mitchell to brief and argue a case as a friend-of-the-court in Bowe v. United States, a case concerning a prisoner’s efforts to secure post-conviction relief, after the parties agreed with each others' positions. The court often turns to former clerks to present arguments in such cases.

items.title: Video no muestra una erupción auténtica del volcán Anak Krakatoa en Indonesia
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Expertos en vulcanología y autoridades en Indonesia dijeron que un video atribuido en redes sociales a una erupción del volcán Anak Krakatoa no coincide con la zona montañosa aislada ni con el paisaje circundante de dicha región.
items.body:
Expertos en vulcanología y autoridades en Indonesia dijeron que un video atribuido en redes sociales a una erupción del volcán Anak Krakatoa no coincide con la zona montañosa aislada ni con el paisaje circundante de dicha región.
Publicaciones en redes sociales difundieron el clip luego de que el Anak Krakatoa hizo erupción y provocó [USN:L4N44X037 TEXT:"cierres temporales"] de aeropuertos y [USN:L4N44Z0IP TEXT:"cancelaciones"] de vuelos el 6 de septiembre.
El volcán se encuentra en una isla deshabitada en el estrecho de Sonda, entre las islas de Java y Sumatra. El asentamiento más cercano está a más de 16 kilómetros y en la propia isla no hay barrios residenciales ni infraestructura como los que aparecen en el video.
Los registros oficiales y las imágenes obtenidas por Reuters desde el lugar muestran el aislamiento geográfico del volcán. Además, los vehículos del video circulan por el lado derecho de la carretera, pese a que en Indonesia se conduce por el lado izquierdo.
ANÁLISIS DE EXPERTOS Heruningtyas Desi Purnamasari, jefa del equipo de volcanes del Centro Indonesio del Vulcanología y Mitigación de Riesgos Geológicos (PVMBG, por sus siglas en indonesio), dijo a Reuters por correo electrónico el 16 de septiembre que el video no es auténtico y no representa las condiciones geográficas ni el entorno aislado del volcán.
Mike Cassidy, profesor asociado de la Universidad de Birmingham y presidente de la Alianza Global para Riesgos Volcánicos, dijo a Reuters en un correo electrónico el 10 de septiembre que el video no coincide con las características del volcán ni de su entorno y que las imágenes fueron generadas con IA.
Tamsin Mather, catedrática de Ciencias de la Tierra en la Universidad de Oxford y especialista en el estudio de gases y procesos atmosféricos durante erupciones volcánicas, dijo a Reuters en un correo enviado en la misma fecha que el video no corresponde al Anak Krakatoa, que está en una isla sin grandes asentamientos cercanos.
La Agencia Nacional de Gestión de Desastres de Indonesia no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios de Reuters.
VEREDICTO Falso. El video no muestra una erupción del volcán Anak Krakatoa en Indonesia. Expertos y autoridades dijeron que las imágenes no coinciden con el entorno auténtico del volcán.

items.title: Vice-ministro das Relações Exteriores da Coreia do Norte participará da Assembleia Geral da ONU na próxima semana, diz Yonhap
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Kim Son-Gyong, vice-ministro das Relações Exteriores da Coreia do Norte, planeja participar de uma sessão de alto nível da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, que deve começar em Nova York na próxima semana, informou a Yonhap na sexta-feira (horário local), citando uma fonte do órgão internacional.
items.body:
Kim Son-Gyong, vice-ministro das Relações Exteriores da Coreia do Norte, planeja participar de uma sessão de alto nível da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, que deve começar em Nova York na próxima semana, informou a Yonhap na sexta-feira (horário local), citando uma fonte do órgão internacional.
Kim deve se reunir com o secretário-geral da ONU, António Guterres, e com autoridades de países amigos da Coreia do Norte, como Cuba e Venezuela, segundo a reportagem da Yonhap.
A Reuters não conseguiu confirmar a notícia imediatamente.

items.title: Saudi Pivots Oil Routes After Pipeline Attack
items.summary: Saudi Arabia is ramping up prompt sales of crude from outside the Strait of Hormuz following the shutdown of the kingdom’s East-West pipeline, which halted cross-country flows to its Red Sea coast. The sale helped attribute to a fall in oil prices as physical markets cooled from recent peaks as traders bet some Middle East supply outages would be short-lived. Noam Raydan, William Sudhaus Senior Fellow at the Washington Institute, joins Bloomberg Businessweek to discuss why the Saudi pipeline is so crucial and what the attack on the pipeline could mean for the broader Saudi oil industry. items.title: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong warns of stronger response to US-led drills
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Friday that U.S.-led multinational military drills such as the Pacific Vanguard naval exercise are the "main source" of worsening tensions on the Korean Peninsula and said there would be "never ever" any change in Pyongyang's course of strengthening its nuclear deterrent.
items.body:
North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Friday that U.S.-led multinational military drills such as the Pacific Vanguard naval exercise are the "main source" of worsening tensions on the Korean Peninsula and said there would be "never ever" any change in Pyongyang's course of strengthening its nuclear deterrent.
In a statement carried by state media KCNA, she also warned North Korea's armed forces would "mobilize all means available" if the country's military sovereignty and security interests were deemed to have been seriously violated.

items.summary: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, ordenou que os ativos na Rússia do grupo alimentício suíço Nestlé e do grupo francês de supermercados Auchan fossem colocados sob administração temporária, de acordo com um decreto presidencial publicado nesta quinta-feira.
items.body:
O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, ordenou que os ativos na Rússia do grupo alimentício suíço Nestlé (NESN.S) e do grupo francês de supermercados Auchan fossem colocados sob administração temporária, de acordo com um decreto presidencial publicado nesta quinta-feira.
O decreto indica que os ativos da Nestlé e da Auchan na Rússia foram transferidos para a administração temporária da L.E.V. Management.
Anteriormente, o jornal Kommersant havia noticiado que uma empresa conhecida como KS Logistika havia solicitado a Putin que colocasse os ativos da Nestlé sob administração temporária.
O Kommersant, citando uma fonte a par do assunto, informou que o pedido abrangia cinco entidades de propriedade da Nestlé na Rússia e poderia, em teoria, resultar em uma mudança de propriedade.
A Nestlé informou à Reuters que não havia sido contatada pelas autoridades russas a respeito do pedido. A empresa afirmou que continuava operando seus escritórios e fábricas na Rússia, cumprindo todas as exigências regulatórias.
A KS Logistika registrou receita de 1,6 milhão de rublos (US$18.735) em 2025 e acredita-se que represente interesses de terceiros, informou o jornal, sem dar mais detalhes.
A Reuters não conseguiu verificar essas informações de forma independente.
A Rússia reforçou o controle sobre ativos de propriedade estrangeira desde o início da guerra na Ucrânia, em 2022. De acordo com um decreto assinado por Putin em 2023, Moscou tem o poder de colocar ativos de países que considera “hostis” sob administração temporária.
Esse mecanismo já foi utilizado anteriormente para assumir o controle das subsidiárias russas de empresas como a Danone e a Carlsberg. A Nestlé continuou operando na Rússia, argumentando que, como produtora de alimentos, fornece bens essenciais.
De acordo com a fonte do Kommersant, o pedido decorre da decisão da Nestlé de não expandir a capacidade de produção na Rússia e de interromper as exportações de produtos fabricados em suas fábricas russas.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [パリ　１７日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[パリ　１７日　ロイター] - 欧州連合（ＥＵ）のフォンデアライエン欧州委員長は１７日、ミサイルとドローン（無人機）の調達に向け、ウクライナに３３億ユーロを拠出すると表明した。 

フォンデアライエン氏はＸへの投稿で、「先ほど（ウクライナの）ゼレンスキー大統領と電話会談を行った。明日（１８日）、ウクライナでのミサイルとドローン調達のために３３億ユーロを拠出する」と述べた。

ゼレンスキー氏はメッセージアプリ「テレグラム」への投稿で、今回の新たな資金拠出については言及しなかったものの、フォンデアライエン氏との会話は「非常に生産的」だったとし、資金調達の問題を含め、「わが国の防衛力強化に向けた極めて重要な措置」に議論が集中したと語った。

items.title: Disney names insider Adam Smith as chairman of streaming business
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Walt Disney on Thursday named insider Adam Smith chairman of its streaming business, as the company seeks to sharpen its focus across its direct-to-consumer platforms such as Disney+ and Hulu.
items.body:
Walt Disney (DIS.N) on Thursday named insider Adam Smith chairman of its streaming business, as the company seeks to sharpen its focus across its direct-to-consumer platforms such as Disney+ and Hulu.
The company also named Joe Earley president of Disney Entertainment Television Franchise and Content Strategy, creating a new role focused on developing television franchises and maximizing their value across the company.
Smith, who joined Disney in 2024, will also be responsible for strategy and development across Disney's global entertainment subscription video-on-demand business, proprietary advertising technology and emerging technologies.
The appointment comes as Disney places greater emphasis on its direct-to-consumer business, which has become a key part of its strategy to distribute content, deepen engagement with viewers and grow its advertising business.
Earley joined Disney in 2019 ahead of the launch of Disney+ and became president of Hulu in 2022.

ORLANDO, Florida, Sept 17 : World stocks paused their recent slide and rebounded strongly on Thursday, and the global bond rout also took a breather, as investors digested the US Federal Reserve's interest rate hike the day before and cheered a second consecutive day of lower oil prices.
In my column today, I posit that US President Donald Trump will probably never see another interest rate as president. As The Rolling Stones famously said, you can't always get what you want. Apparently, not even if you're the most powerful person in the world.
Today's Key Reads
• Investors are gaining more confidence in the Federal Reserve's inflation-fighting backbone, but uncertainty about how far it will raise interest rates to keep prices in check is likely to cause volatility for stocks and bonds in the weeks ahead.

• On Wednesday, US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh became his predecessor, Jerome Powell. Perhaps not in his own eyes or in the eyes of investors, but, crucially, to the White House that appointed him. The central bank announced an increase in the federal funds rate, and a clear intent to lower inflation, perhaps through further hikes. That won’t please Trump, who thinks rates should be “1 per cent, or less”. The administration’s campaign for easy money and against Federal Reserve independence is now likely to return in earnest.
• The Bank of England kept interest rates on hold on Thursday but warned they might have to go up if the Iran war drags on, while predicting British inflation will top 4 per cent early next year.
• The Bank of Japan is set to raise interest rates to a 31-year high on Friday and signal readiness to keep pushing up borrowing costs, joining other major central banks in fighting persistent inflation pressures driven by soaring oil costs.
• The US Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday unveiled its long-awaited exemption that will allow companies to offer trading in blockchain-based or "tokenized" stocks and other securities, in a major move that could integrate digital assets more deeply into traditional markets.
• Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: MSCI World +0.7 per cent, Europe, UK both up around 1 per cent, best day since July. On Wall Street, Dow +0.6 per cent, S&P 500 +1 per cent, Nasdaq +1.7 per cent.SECTORS/SHARES: Nine sectors on the S&P 500 rise, two fall. Tech +2.2 per cent, consumer discretionary +1.5 per cent. Energy -0.1 per cent. "SOX" chip index +3 per cent.FX: Dollar breaks 6-day winning streak. NZ dollar among biggest gainers.BONDS: Bonds mostly rebound, US curves still flatten a little. UK 30-year yield slides 12 bps on BoE QT news.COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil -1 per cent, WTI briefly dips below $100. Average US diesel nudges $6.40/gallon. Gold +2 per cent, biggest rise in a month.
Today's Talking Points:
The morning after the night before
Investors around the world have had a chance to digest the Fed's rate hike, and more significantly, its "dot plot" signals and Warsh's press conference. It was a "buy the rumor, sell the fact" kind of day — short-covering and profit-taking meant stocks and bonds mostly rose, oil fell, and worries over inflation, long bonds, or the Fed falling behind the curve were put to one side. For now.
Does this relief quickly fizzle? While the Fed has taken a hawkish turn, the anticipated hiking cycle of around 100 bps in total, as per current market pricing, would be the shallowest in history. Maybe that's how it pans out. On the other hand, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model is pointing to 5.1 per cent growth in Q3, which would be the strongest non-pandemic-distorted quarter since 2000. Growth sentiment on the FOMC is strong too — not one of the 18 policymakers who contributed to the latest Summary of Economic Projections sees downside risks to growth.
Gilt trip
The Bank of England on Thursday unveiled plans for how it intends to offload most of the remaining £488 billion of bonds on its balance sheet by 2034. That longer-term plan might weigh on the gilt market, but the Bank's more immediate plans were much more warmly received — the BoE will pause bond sales for the next six months, and halt sales of long-dated gilts entirely.
Along with US Treasury's plans to triple the size of scheduled buybacks of long-dated Treasuries, the BoE's tweak reflects growing concerns among global policymakers over the elevated level of long-term borrowing costs. Earlier this week, the 30-year gilt yield reached 5.95 per cent, the highest since 1998. The 30-year yield tumbled 12 bps on Thursday, its biggest fall since May. So, immediate relief. But will it last?
Oh Canada
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney seems to be enjoying his tour of Europe, taking in a football match in Liverpool with UK PM Andy Burnham on Wednesday, and drawing laughs and warm applause for his speech to the European Parliament on Thursday. One suspects Trump is rather less impressed, and on Wednesday the US President threatened trade sanctions in response to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's proposal to create a new status for the EU-Canada relationship.
Carney did not adopt von der Leyen's term "associate member", but he clearly wants to forge stronger, closer trade ties across the Atlantic. Little wonder, perhaps, as the US-Canada trade war shows no sign of cooling. Asked about Trump's threats, Carney said: "Canadians are united that nobody is going to tell us what language we speak. No one is going to dictate our culture or with whom we can strike agreements internationally." Neither Trump nor Carney seem to be backing down. Not publicly, at least.
What could move markets tomorrow?
• Japan interest rate decision
• Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock speaks
• UK retail sales (August)
• Germany PPI inflation (August)
• US Federal Reserve officials scheduled to speak include vice chair for supervision Michelle Bowman and Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid

items.title: What will Trump and Xi discuss in Washington next week?
items.author: David Brunnstrom, Joe Cash
items.creator: David Brunnstrom, Joe Cash
items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump will welcome Chinese leader Xi Jinping next week for their second meeting this year, as the two leaders seek stability in a relationship under pressure over issues ranging from trade to Taiwan and Iran to global worries about artificial intelligence.
items.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump will welcome Chinese leader Xi Jinping next week for their second meeting this year, as the two leaders seek stability in a relationship under pressure over issues ranging from trade to Taiwan and Iran to global worries about artificial intelligence.
Xi arrives for his first White House visit in a decade at the helm of an economy on track to post a $1 trillion trade surplus for a second straight year. Trump, mired in the Iran war and with low approval ratings, is looking for trade wins he can tout to Americans unhappy with rising prices.
Here are some of the key issues for the September 24 summit, which follows [USN:L1N41S10X TEXT:"Trump's May visit to Beijing"]:
TRADE TRUCE OR BACK TO TRADE WAR? Markets will watch for signs of an extension of a tariff truce announced after [USN:L1N3WB17J TEXT:"a Trump-Xi summit in South Korea last October and set to expire on November 10"]. That deal paused a trade war in which the world's two largest economies threatened global supply chains with tit-for-tat tariffs that topped 100%.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said this month the countries will make [USN:L6N44Z0GE TEXT:""some announcements on agriculture and non-tariff barriers"]" and traders will be watching for progress on an agreed mutual tariff reduction covering $30 billion in goods — a step China could most easily take by cutting duties on U.S. agricultural imports.
U.S. officials say they have continued to press China to address its lack of compliance with last year's agreement, while Beijing has pressed for further tariff relief.
JETS, FARM PRODUCE AND TECH Trump will be looking to announce trade wins ahead of November midterm congressional elections, including by locking in high-profile purchases of Boeing aircraft and agricultural products.
Sources told Reuters this month that Xi is [USN:L6N44W15F TEXT:"preparing a large business delegation to accompany him"] similar to 2015, when China signed a $38 billion agreement for 300 Boeing (BA.N) aircraft. China said after the May summit that [USN:L1N41X04M TEXT:"it would buy 200 more Boeing jets"] and the company said this was only an "initial tranche" of a [USN:L8N42502K TEXT:"potentially far bigger deal"].
China has been in prolonged talks with Boeing for a transaction that industry sources say could include 500 737 MAX jets, plus dozens of wide-body planes, a deal stalled for years as Trump has [USN:L6N41511X TEXT:"threatened to cut off China's access to critical spare engine parts"].
Beijing has been pressing the US to further delay a rule that would bar thousands of Chinese firms from receiving [USN:L6N42P0KD TEXT:"advanced "]US technology, while Washington wants Beijing to [USN:L1N43W1DL TEXT:"ease shipments of rare earths and critical minerals"] used in high-tech applications from automobile to aerospace manufacturing, as well as defense.
IRAN WAR The two presidents are expected to discuss the Iran war, which Trump has struggled to end after launching it with Israel in February.
China maintains close ties to Tehran and is by far the world's biggest buyer of Iranian oil exports. Washington sees Xi as uniquely able to exert pressure on Tehran, but he has shown little inclination to do so. Reuters last month reported that Beijing is selling billions of dollars' worth of goods to Iran through a [USN:L6N43P11D TEXT:"sanctions-evasion scheme"]. China's foreign ministry says it is not aware of such a scheme.
Despite U.S. frustration, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stopped short of imposing penalties on Chinese banks when he last month unveiled an "economic onslaught" against Iran and warned countries to cut business ties with Tehran.
Bessent has said he would meet Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng this weekend and that Trump and Xi [USN:L1N4570NX TEXT:"would continue discussions on China's financial ties to Tehran"] during the summit.
On Sunday, Trump [USN:L8N4550G3 TEXT:"brushed aside a report that Iran acquired satellite images of a base in Jordan from Chinese entities"] before an attack that killed three U.S. troops there in July.
TAIWAN China has long been hoping to extract concessions from Trump over Taiwan, a democratically governed island Beijing claims as its own, and the world's leading producer of cutting-edge chips. Taiwan strongly objects to China’s sovereignty claims and says only the island’s people can decide their future.
U.S. law requires the administration to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, but [USN:L1N41S025 TEXT:"questions have been hanging"] over a [USN:L1N42X0T0 TEXT:"large pending arms package"] worth up to $14 billion since Trump's Beijing visit.
People familiar with Chinese efforts told Reuters Beijing hopes to persuade Trump to state publicly that the U.S. opposes Taiwan's independence instead of saying only that it does not support independence, which has been Washington's formulation for decades.
Any U.S. shift on Taiwan would be highly controversial, raising questions about Washington's resolve to defend the island, alarming allies across Asia and provoking opposition in Congress.
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE Analysts see artificial intelligence as a potential area for cooperation, given its implications for national security, economic competitiveness and military capabilities, and shared U.S. and Chinese concerns about misuse. However, experts say intense competition in the field between the countries is likely to limit the scope for anything beyond symbolic agreements.
On Wednesday, Axios cited a statement from Bessent as saying that the United States [USN:L1N4580OA TEXT:"was open to discussing shared risks with China"] in AI talks this weekend.
[USN:L1N45403R TEXT:"US lawmakers have urged new rules to govern AI"] systems, while Dario Amodei, chief executive of U.S. artificial-intelligence firm Anthropic, warned this month that Chinese dominance in AI could pose security risks to the United States.
Chinese state media dismissed Amodei's warning as coming from a "Cold War playbook" while Trump has [USN:L1N4560HH TEXT:"brushed aside calls to slow AI development"], saying that "very negative forces" were raising exaggerated concerns.
FENTANYL FLOWS Curbing the flow of fentanyl precursor chemicals from China remains a concern of the Trump administration, given the ravages the drug has caused among Americans.
Washington has repeatedly accused Beijing of failing to stem the flow of precursors, and Trump imposed fentanyl-related tariffs on China in early 2025 that the U.S. Supreme Court struck down in February.
FBI Director Kash Patel told Reuters last month that he had [USN:L6N44215F TEXT:"forged a new law enforcement partnership with China"] in hopes of curbing the trade.

items.title: Trading Day: Lower oil, yields boost stocks
items.author: Jamie McGeever
items.creator: Jamie McGeever
items.summary: World stocks paused their recent slide and rebounded strongly on Thursday, and the global bond rout also took a breather, as investors digested the US Federal Reserve's interest rate hike the day before and cheered a second consecutive day of lower oil prices.
items.body:
World stocks [USN:L4N4581RL TEXT:"paused"] their recent slide and rebounded strongly on Thursday, and the global bond rout also took a breather, as investors digested the US Federal Reserve's interest rate hike the day before and cheered a second consecutive day of [USN:L4N4581LH TEXT:"lower oil prices"].
In my column today, I posit that US President Donald Trump will probably never see another interest rate as president. As The Rolling Stones famously said, [USN:L6N45818V TEXT:"you can't always get what you want"]. Apparently, not even if you're the most powerful person in the world.
Today's Key Reads
Investors are gaining more confidence in the Federal Reserve's inflation-fighting backbone, but uncertainty about how far it will raise interest rates to keep prices in check is [USN:L6N4570U9 TEXT:"likely to cause volatility"] for stocks and bonds in the weeks ahead.
On Wednesday, US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh became his predecessor, Jerome Powell. Perhaps not in his own eyes or in the eyes of investors, but, crucially, to the White House that appointed him. The central bank announced an increase in the federal funds rate, and a clear intent to lower inflation, perhaps through further hikes. That won’t please Trump, who thinks rates should be “1%, or less”. The [USN:L6N45814H TEXT:"administration’s campaign for easy money"] and against Federal Reserve independence is now likely to return in earnest.
The [USN:L8N4590W3 TEXT:"Bank of England"] kept interest rates on hold on Thursday but warned they might have to go up if the Iran war drags on, while predicting British inflation will top 4% early next year.
The Bank of Japan is set to raise interest rates to a [USN:L4N4561PU TEXT:"31-year high"] on Friday and signal readiness to keep pushing up borrowing costs, joining other major central banks in fighting persistent inflation pressures driven by soaring oil costs.
The US Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday unveiled its long-awaited exemption that will allow companies to offer trading in blockchain-based or "tokenized" stocks and other securities, in a major move that [USN:L1N4470NU TEXT:"could integrate digital assets more deeply into traditional markets"].
Today's Key Market Moves
STOCKS: MSCI World +0.7%, [USN:L4N4590H9 TEXT:"Europe"], [USN:L6N4590IN TEXT:"UK"] both up around 1%, best day since July. On Wall Street, Dow +0.6%, S&P 500 +1%, Nasdaq +1.7%.
SECTORS/SHARES: Nine sectors on the S&P 500 rise, two fall. Tech +2.2%, consumer discretionary +1.5%. Energy -0.1%. "SOX" chip index +3%.
FX: [USN:L4N459050 TEXT:"Dollar"] breaks 6-day winning streak. [USN:AZN4TKHFU TEXT:"NZ dollar"] among biggest gainers.
BONDS: Bonds mostly rebound, US curves still flatten a little. UK 30-year yield slides 12 bps on [USN:L8N4590WV TEXT:"BoE QT"] news.
COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N4581LH TEXT:"Oil"] -1%, WTI briefly dips below $100. Average US diesel nudges $6.40/gallon. [USN:L4N4581TB TEXT:"Gold"] +2%, biggest rise in a month.

Today's Talking Points:
The morning after the night before
Investors around the world have had a chance to digest the Fed's rate hike, and more significantly, its "dot plot" signals and Warsh's press conference. It was a "buy the rumor, sell the fact" kind of day — short-covering and profit-taking meant stocks and bonds mostly rose, oil fell, and worries over inflation, long bonds, or the Fed falling behind the curve were put to one side. For now.
Does this relief quickly fizzle? While the Fed has taken a hawkish turn, the anticipated hiking cycle of around 100 bps in total, as per current market pricing, would be the shallowest in history. Maybe that's how it pans out. On the other hand, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model is pointing to 5.1% growth in Q3, which would be the strongest non-pandemic-distorted quarter since 2000. Growth sentiment on the FOMC is strong too — not one of the 18 policymakers who contributed to the latest Summary of Economic Projections sees downside risks to growth.
Gilt trip
The Bank of England on Thursday [USN:L8N4590WV TEXT:"unveiled plans"] for how it intends to offload most of the remaining £488 billion of bonds on its balance sheet by 2034. That longer-term plan might weigh on the gilt market, but the Bank's more immediate plans were much more [USN:L8N4590VA TEXT:"warmly received"] — the BoE will pause bond sales for the next six months, and halt sales of long-dated gilts entirely.
Along with US Treasury's plans to triple the size of scheduled buybacks of long-dated Treasuries, the BoE's tweak reflects growing concerns among global policymakers over the elevated level of long-term borrowing costs. Earlier this week, the 30-year gilt yield reached 5.95%, the highest since 1998. The 30-year yield tumbled 12 bps on Thursday, its biggest fall since May. So, immediate relief. But will it last?
Oh Canada
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney seems to be enjoying his tour of Europe, taking in a football match in Liverpool with UK PM Andy Burnham on Wednesday, and drawing laughs and warm applause for his speech to the [USN:L8N4590UA TEXT:"European Parliament"] on Thursday. One suspects Trump is rather less impressed, and on Wednesday the US President threatened trade sanctions in response to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's proposal to create a new status for the EU-Canada relationship.
Carney did not adopt von der Leyen's term "associate member", but he clearly wants to forge stronger, closer trade ties across the Atlantic. Little wonder, perhaps, as the US-Canada trade war shows [USN:L6N4580Y1 TEXT:"no sign of cooling"]. Asked about Trump's threats, Carney said: "Canadians are united that nobody is going to tell us what language we speak. No one is going to dictate our culture or with whom we can [USN:B5N44300X TEXT:"strike agreements"] internationally." Neither Trump nor Carney seem to be backing down. Not publicly, at least.
What could move markets tomorrow?

Germany PPI inflation (August)

items.title: 個人向け国債の発行、金利高で過去最高ペース－安定消化へ家計に期待
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 国内の金利上昇を背景に、預貯金よりも利率が高い個人向け国債の発行が拡大している。潤沢な家計マネーが国債の安定消化を支える資金として存在感を見せ始めた。

ブルームバーグがまとめたデータによると、4－9月期の個人向け国債発行額は前年同期比で84%増え、年度上期として過去最高の5兆1390億円に膨らんだ。

日本銀行が国債買い入れを縮小し、インフレ懸念が利回りを押し上げる中、市場では巨額の国債発行を誰が買い支えるのかを巡って議論が続いている。年金積立金管理運用独立行政法人（GPIF）が国内債券の配分を引き上げるとの観測が強まる一方、政府は1132兆円の現預金を抱える家計からの資金取り込みを模索している。

バークレイズ証券の門田真一郎為替債券調査部長は、家計は多額の預貯金を保有するため「誰が国債を消化していくかという観点では、GPIFよりも重要なトピック」だと指摘。家計の購入が増えれば、市場に供給される国債が減り、機関投資家だけが買い手となる場合に比べて「市場の金利は上がりにくくなるだろう」と話す。

日銀の統計によると、家計の国債保有残高は2026年6月末時点で21兆9434億円と、22年末から73%増加した。ただ、家計が保有する現預金に対する比率は1.9%にとどまり、08年に付けた過去最高水準の4.5%を大きく下回る。仮にこの比率が当時の水準まで回復する場合、家計は国債を28兆5000億円程度追加購入することになり、これは今年度の国債市中発行額（短期国債を除く）の22%に相当する計算になる。

三菱UFJアセットマネジメントの八木孝幸商品マーケティング企画部長は「機関投資家が果たしている役割は依然として大きく、個人投資家が短期間で代替するとは考えていない」と言う。その上で、個人投資家は国債市場の安定的な買い手の一角として徐々に存在感を高め、「投資家基盤の多様化や市場の安定性向上に寄与する可能性がある」とみている。

items.title: 米、イラン高官の国連総会出席認める　パレスチナ議長には再びビザ発給拒否
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Simon Lewis

[１７日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Simon Lewis

[１７日 ロイター] - 米国務省は１７日、来週ニューヨークで開かれる国連総会にイラン政府高官の出席を認める方針であると明らかにした。米国とイランが依然として交戦状態にあり、紛争終結に向けた断続的な協議が続いている中での対応となる。

国務省報道官は、国連本部が置かれる米国の義務に沿って、「イラン政権の中核となる代表団」の会議出席を認めると説明。その上で「われわれの方針に基づき、代表団には渡航制限が課され、ぜいたく品などの購入は禁止される。代表団の規模は昨年よりも小規模だ」と述べた。

決定に詳しい関係筋によると、ペゼシュキアン大統領やアラグチ外相を含む高官に査証（ビザ）が発給される。 

イラン外務省はロイターのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

また、国連総会は１７日、パレスチナ自治政府のアッバス議長が国連年次総会でビデオ演説することを認める決議を採択した。米国が同議長へのビザ発給を再び拒否したことを受けたもので、２年連続の措置となる。 

決議は賛成１５２、反対３で可決され、４カ国が棄権した。アッバス氏と他のパレスチナ高官が米国への渡航を阻まれた場合、今後１年間はビデオを通じて国連の会議や会合に参加することも認められる。

米国のブルース国連次席大使は採決前、総会で「パレスチナ自治政府がパートナーとして扱われることを望むなら、テロへの資金援助をやめ、真剣な統治の代わりに外交上のパフォーマンスを利用するのをやめなければならない」と述べた。

パレスチナのマンスール国連大使は、パレスチナ指導部は米国によるビザ発給拒否の措置を拒絶し、非難していると述べた。

１９４７年の国連「本部協定」に基づき、米国は原則として、外国の外交官がニューヨークの国連本部へ立ち入ることを許可しなければならない。しかし、米政府は、安全保障、過激主義、外交政策上の理由からビザの発給を拒否できるとしている。

items.title: EUA vão permitir que líderes iranianos participem da Assembleia Geral da ONU
items.author: Simon Lewis
items.creator: Simon Lewis
items.summary: O governo Trump vai permitir que altas autoridades iranianas participem da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas em Nova York na próxima semana, informou o Departamento de Estado nesta quinta-feira, mesmo com Washington e Teerã ainda em conflito, mas em negociações intermitentes com o objetivo de encerrar a guerra.
items.body:
O governo Trump vai permitir que altas autoridades iranianas participem da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas em Nova York na próxima semana, informou o Departamento de Estado nesta quinta-feira, mesmo com Washington e Teerã ainda em conflito, mas em negociações intermitentes com o objetivo de encerrar a guerra.
Um porta-voz do Departamento de Estado afirmou que uma “delegação principal do regime iraniano” teria permissão para participar da reunião, em conformidade com as obrigações dos Estados Unidos como país anfitrião do órgão internacional.
Isso significa que autoridades como o presidente iraniano Masoud Pezeshkian e o ministro das Relações Exteriores Abbas Araqchi receberão vistos, segundo uma fonte a par da decisão.
O governo do presidente Donald Trump vem tendo negociações intermitentes com os líderes do Irã com o objetivo de pôr fim à guerra que começou em 28 de fevereiro, quando os EUA e Israel atacaram o Irã. Teerã respondeu com ataques a Israel e a países do Golfo que abrigam bases norte-americanas.
“A delegação estará sujeita a restrições de viagem e enfrentará proibições quanto à compra de artigos de luxo e outros bens, de acordo com nossa política. A delegação é menor do que a do ano passado”, acrescentou o porta-voz do Departamento de Estado.
No passado, o governo dos EUA impediu a delegação iraniana de entrar em lojas e restringiu seus deslocamentos entre a sede das Nações Unidas, a missão iraniana na ONU, a residência do embaixador iraniano na ONU e o Aeroporto John F. Kennedy, em Nova York.
O Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Irã não respondeu imediatamente a pedido de comentário da Reuters.
De acordo com o “acordo de sede” da ONU de 1947, os Estados Unidos são, em geral, obrigados a permitir o acesso de diplomatas estrangeiros às Nações Unidas. Mas Washington afirma que pode negar vistos por motivos de “segurança, terrorismo e política externa”.
O governo Trump anunciou na quarta-feira que negaria a entrada de autoridades palestinas para a reunião da ONU, prorrogando uma proibição em vigor desde o ano passado, devido a ações que tomaram para “internacionalizar o conflito israelo-palestino”, incluindo a apresentação de processos contra Israel em tribunais internacionais.
O presidente palestino Mahmoud Abbas teve seu visto negado como parte da medida dos EUA, afirmou uma autoridade palestina.

items.body:
The US Federal Reserve nudged interest rates higher by a quarter of a percentage point on Wednesday, the first rate hike in more than three years. My colleagues report that while investors are gaining more confidence in the Fed's inflation-fighting backbone, uncertainty about how far it will raise interest rates to keep prices in check is likely to cause volatility for stocks and bonds in the weeks ahead.
So how will it impact your wallet?
If you’re sitting on cash, you’ll be able to earn more on your savings. But if you’re juggling any variable-rate debt, you need to be strategic. (We have an adjustable-rate mortgage, so I follow rates very carefully!)
Either way, read my latest article for Reuters , and let me know how higher rates will impact you via the link in my bio.

RENT VERSUS BUY As young professionals watch their retirement and investment accounts compound, many are asking: Does it make more sense to keep that money working in the market, or tie it up in a down payment and a mortgage?
Young adults are less likely than older adults to say buying a home is a “very good” investment, according to a 2026 Pew Research Center survey, which found that just 37% of renter households younger than 40 could afford the monthly cost of owning a home in 2024, down from 56% in 2019.
Older generations tend to see renting as a waste of money. But for Gen Z, it’s a wealth-building strategy with a bigger payoff.
Here is why young buyers say renting and investing beats buying a home .
Do you agree? Let me know if renting is the smarter money move via the link in my bio.
READER MAILBAG In response to my recent article about [USN:L6N44H16N TEXT:"love and money"], I received this message from reader Steven Foster of Anacortes, Washington, which is slightly edited for space reasons:
I know I am now considered old fashioned, but my wife and I got married in 1973 and went through a lot of stages with our finances.
The underlying principle has always been the same. There is no such thing as hers or mine, there is only ours.
I was the major bread winner, but if things got tight, she just didn’t have enough to do and was bored, or we had a special project and needed extra money, she would get a job and help out.
Now, as we get older, it still holds true. If something comes up, and we have to spend money on either one of us, it is just money – and not hers or mine, just money needed to be spent.
In retirement, there is only one pool, well four accounts because of retirement accounts, but one total available pool. We live accordingly.
This has taken a lot of stress out of our lives over the years as we never have the yours or mine issues to fight over or argue about. It has kept us very close together as with the money being only one pot, we are just one couple and we live as one unit.
I believe that if more couples would live this way there would be less divorce and happier lives.
And in response to my article about [USN:L6N44S11W TEXT:"setting a budget for college"] spending, I received this comment from Diana Bruce of Washington, D.C., also edited a wee bit:
I had my kids use the money from their summer jobs to pay for their daily expenses during the school year. And their paychecks were direct-deposited into their savings accounts. It felt important from a youth development perspective to have my kids in charge of spending the money they made — and not have it go into some “college” pot they didn’t manage.
The summer before college, I had each kid make a list of every item they used in a day/week/month, and research how much each costs. Then I sat with them to build a monthly budget and add their usual spending on fun stuff. They decided how much they needed every month, and then we set up a monthly automatic transfer from savings to checking at the end of each month that they used for their spending money and daily expenses.
They were not responsible for tuition, housing, meal plan/grocery budget, utilities, trips home or medical expenses. Well, one kid was responsible for housing the last two years and got a resident assistant job!
I added them as authorized users on my credit card halfway through college, once I had faith that they could follow my rules for usage — these were individual decisions based on each kid’s readiness. I remember getting into credit card debt with one of those cards they promoted on campus when I was young, and I recommended that my kids delay their own card until they’re done with college and making their own money — more maturity and more experience managing money.
Both are now out of college and know how to manage their money because they learned it with monthly practice and guardrails that lowered over time. And they learned it at their own pace, because they’re both very different.
Share your money story with me via the link in my bio!

items.title: Ocean container shipping rates could test record highs as Iran war fuel spike drives rise, analysts say
items.author: Lisa Baertlein
items.creator: Lisa Baertlein
items.summary: The off-contract ocean container shipping rate from China to the U.S. East Coast has returned to levels seen after COVID-19 upended global trade, and could set new record highs as the U.S. and Israeli war on Iran drives fuel costs higher.
items.body:
The off-contract ocean container shipping rate from China to the U.S. East Coast has returned to levels seen after COVID-19 upended global trade, and could set new record highs as the U.S. and Israeli war on Iran drives fuel costs higher.
The spot rates on that route hit $10,948 per 40-foot container, more than quadrupling since the start of the Iran war on February 28, according to data from freight pricing platform Xeneta.
"That leaves freight rates on these critical trades just short of the all-time high set during the COVID-19 disruption," Peter Sand, Xeneta's chief analyst, said of the route, where rates hit a record $11,900 in January 2022. The Shanghai to New York route is among the busiest and most profitable for global container carriers, including MSC, Maersk (MAERSKb.CO) , COSCO and CMA CGM.
Crude oil prices soared after hostilities intensified with the [USN:L6N451042 TEXT:"U.S. and Iran attacking and sinking some oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz"] and Saudi Arabia closing its vital East-West pipeline due to aerial attacks in the widening Middle East war .
Those events pushed up the global 20-port average price for the very low sulphur fuel oil, known as bunker, used by many container ships. It hit $901.50 per metric ton on Thursday, up from $543.50 per metric ton on February 27 but still below the March 20 peak of $1,053 per metric ton, according to marine fuel price publisher Ship & Bunker. Container ship owners recoup those higher costs via [USN:L6N43N13L TEXT:"surcharges"] and other pricing tools.
"With bunker prices pushing fuel surcharges higher, surpassing the pandemic peak cannot be ruled out," Sand said of the China to East Coast container spot rate. A new record would most likely come this month, with the traditional Golden Week [USN:L6N45118F TEXT:"volume spike"] driven by shippers, including Walmart (WMT.O) and Amazon.com (AMZN.O) rushing goods out of China before factories close in early October for a mandatory holiday break, he said.
Week-over-week spot rates from Shanghai to New York jumped nearly 7% to $10,394 per 40-foot container, according to the Drewry World Container Index (WCI) data on Thursday.
Drewry also expects Golden Week shipments to send the rate higher.
Drewry and Xeneta use different methodologies for their data on spot rates, which, depending on market dynamics, can apply to around half of cargo on the water.
Drewry's WCI Shanghai to New York spot rate [USN:L1N2QX21I TEXT:"peaked"] at $16,000 early in the pandemic when homebound consumers were using federal incentive money to splurge on furniture, big-screen televisions and home exercise equipment.

items.title: 原油続落、ブレントは104ドル台－中東での供給混乱に緩和の兆し
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 17日の原油相場は続落。中東での供給混乱が一部緩和する兆しが引き続き材料視された。一方、戦争に伴う需給逼迫（ひっぱく）がなお続く可能性も意識されている。

北海ブレント11月限は前日比1.01ドル（1%）安の1バレル＝104.82ドル。ウェスト・テキサス・インターミディエート（WTI）10月限は52セント（0.5%）安の101.91ドルで終了した。

前日に、サウジアラビアが東西横断の石油パイプラインについて、輸送能力のおよそ半分を数日以内に回復させることを目指していると報じられた。これを受け、原油供給減少への懸念が一部和らいだ。

中国はサウジからの要請を受けて、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派を抑制するための協力をイランに求めた。ロイター通信が伝えた。

ただ、CIBCプライベート・ウェルス・グループの上級エネルギートレーダー、レベッカ・バビン氏によると、需給は依然として逼迫し、それが原油相場を下支えしている。米国とイランの戦争が中東のエネルギー供給を妨げ、ロシアとウクライナの紛争も長期化する中、リスクはなお多い。

状況がさらに悪化する可能性もある。トランプ米大統領はアクシオスに対し、来週ニューヨークで予定されている湾岸諸国首脳との会談を前に、イランへの攻撃を再び激化させるかどうかについて「大きな決断」が近づいていると述べた。

この日の原油相場下落には、最近の上昇を受けた利益確定売りも一部影響している。

ASグローバル・リスク・マネジメントのチーフアナリスト、アルネ・ローマン・ラスムセン氏は「原油と石油製品全般で押し目買いの好機とみている」と指摘。「価格は下落したが、根底にある供給リスクがなくなったわけではない」と述べた。

原題：Oil Dips Amid Saudi Pipeline Repairs, Supply Concerns（抜粋）

items.title: England beat Sri Lanka by six wickets to secure T20 series 2-0
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Jos Buttler became the first batsman to score 15,000 career T20 runs and Liam Dawson took a three-wicket haul as a dominant England beat Sri Lanka by six wickets in Cardiff on Thursday to secure the series 2-0.
items.body:
Jos Buttler became the first batsman to score 15,000 career T20 runs and Liam Dawson took a three-wicket haul as a dominant England beat Sri Lanka by six wickets in Cardiff on Thursday to secure the series 2-0.
The hosts won [USN:L6N4571AA TEXT:"Tuesday's first T20 in Southampton"] by 119 runs and followed it up on an overcast evening with a 14th consecutive victory over Sri Lanka in the format.
Set a target of 146, after winning the toss and opting to bowl at a murky and overcast Sophia Gardens, England had marched to 48-0 after four overs but openers Aneurin Donald (21) and Buttler (30) then walked in quick succession for 55-2.
Big-hitting captain Harry Brook smashed three sixes in one over but went for 23, well caught by a diving Eshan Malinga off a Wanindu Hasaranga delivery, before Tom Banton steadied the ship with a top scoring 52 not out from 24 balls as England cantered towards another easy win with 47 balls and 7.5 overs to spare.
"Tonight was a special performance, very clinical. Sri Lanka got off to a flier but the way we fought back with the ball was outstanding," said Brook.
"The way Dawson reads the game was outstanding, too."
RIDICULOUS MILESTONE FOR BUTTLER Buttler reached his career 15,000 with a single and Brook said his milestone was simply ridiculous.
"Long may it continue. He has been phenomenal for 15 years and someone you want by your side and in the changing room," he added.
Sri Lanka posted 145 for 9 from their 20 overs, an improvement on their previous 135 all out in 19, with opener Pathum Nissanka hitting 37 from 21 balls.
They had carved out a promising 56-0 but lost momentum with Jamie Overton taking the first wicket with a leaping catch off Player of the Match Dawson, who took his second wicket with the next ball of the sixth over and ended with figures of 3-32.
Jofra Archer (2-34) returned for his 50th T20 cap after being rested for the first T20 of the series, with fellow-seamer Josh Tongue dropping out, and took two wickets in the final over with Dushmantha Chameera bowled middle stump for a duck and Tharindu Rathnayake caught by Brook.
Sonny Baker had another excellent evening with the ball, finishing 1-15 from his four overs with a wicket maiden in the 19th.
Donald, playing on home Welsh soil after making his debut in Southampton, dropped Dasun Shanaka but made up for it with a catch three deliveries later for Dawson's third wicket.
"They were too good. We have to improve a lot, honestly, because we are not up to the mark right now," said Sri Lanka captain Charith Asalanka.
The final T20 of the three-match series is at Manchester's Old Trafford on Saturday.

items.title: Xenon pauses new enrollment in depression, bipolar disorder trials over side-effect concerns
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Xenon Pharmaceuticals on Thursday said it has temporarily paused enrolling new patients in clinical studies testing its experimental drug for major depression and bipolar disorder, following reports of mental and nervous system-related side effects.
items.body:
Xenon Pharmaceuticals (XENE.O) on Thursday said it has temporarily paused enrolling new patients in clinical studies testing its experimental drug for major depression and bipolar disorder, following reports of mental and nervous system-related side effects.
Shares of the drug developer tumbled more than 20% in after-hours trading.
The voluntary pause was a precaution taken after consultations with its safety monitoring board and analyzing adverse events across the trials, Xenon said.
Patients already enrolled in the trials will continue their treatment.
The studies are testing azetukalner, an experimental treatment that is also being developed for epilepsy.
Xenon noted that while the severity and frequency of the side effects aligned with how the drug worked, they had not appeared in an earlier mid-stage study for depression.
The company is now evaluating potential dose adjustments to help reduce the side effects and improve tolerability.
Xenon said the pause does not impact its epilepsy program, and that it has submitted an application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration seeking approval for the drug to treat focal seizures, the most common form of epilepsy.

items.title: Petróleo fecha em queda de 1%, mas se mantém acima de US$100 por barril
items.author: Arathy Somasekhar
items.creator: Arathy Somasekhar
items.summary: Os preços do petróleo fecharam com queda de cerca de 1% nesta quinta-feira, mas permaneceram acima de US$100 o barril, à medida que os investidores avaliavam os impactos dos ataques na Arábia Saudita e dos houthis do Iêmen — apoiados pelo Irã — em contraposição a relatos de que barris adicionais de petróleo saudita poderiam chegar aos mercados globais e amenizar as preocupações com a oferta.
items.body:
Os preços do petróleo fecharam com queda de cerca de 1% nesta quinta-feira, mas permaneceram acima de US$100 o barril, à medida que os investidores avaliavam os impactos dos ataques na Arábia Saudita e dos houthis do Iêmen — apoiados pelo Irã — em contraposição a relatos de que barris adicionais de petróleo saudita poderiam chegar aos mercados globais e amenizar as preocupações com a oferta.
A Arábia Saudita e os houthis do Iêmen, apoiados pelo Irã, trocaram novos ataques através da fronteira nesta quinta-feira, com a propagação da guerra no Oriente Médio para o Iêmen e a Arábia Saudita ameaçando agravar a escassez global de energia causada desde que os Estados Unidos e Israel atacaram o Irã em fevereiro.
Os futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam em queda de US$1,01, ou 0,95%, a US$104,82 por barril, enquanto os futuros do West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos EUA caíram 52 centavos, ou 0,5%, para US$101,91 por barril. Ambos os índices de referência haviam caído cerca de 3% na quarta-feira.
O Brent havia caído mais de US$3 no início do pregão, atingindo seu menor nível desde 10 de setembro, enquanto o WTI também caiu mais de US$3, atingindo seu menor nível desde 11 de setembro, após relatos de que a Arábia Saudita estava oferecendo mais cargas de petróleo às refinarias asiáticas por meio de transferências de navio para navio ao largo do porto de Sohar, em Omã. Isso compensará parte da interrupção causada pelos ataques ao oleoduto Leste-Oeste que leva ao Mar Vermelho.
A Arábia Saudita também buscava restaurar cerca de metade da capacidade de seu oleoduto Leste-Oeste em poucos dias, após a interrupção da operação na semana passada devido a ataques com drones, informou a Bloomberg.
Os preços do petróleo haviam subido para níveis próximos às máximas de quatro meses nesta semana, depois que fontes do setor de transporte marítimo informaram que os embarques de petróleo no centro de exportação de Yanbu, na Arábia Saudita, no Mar Vermelho, haviam sido suspensos e que Riade havia cancelado algumas entregas de cargas para clientes europeus. O oleoduto Leste-Oeste abastece Yanbu.
Operadores do mercado afirmaram que um fechamento prolongado do oleoduto poderia reduzir em até 4% o abastecimento global de petróleo. A Arábia Saudita não informou quando as operações poderão ser retomadas, mas Wright disse à CNBC na terça-feira que o petróleo deve voltar a fluir pelo oleoduto em poucos dias.

items.body:
Os contratos futuros da soja negociados na bolsa de Chicago fecharam com variações mínimas nesta quinta-feira, com os contratos mais ativos de curto prazo registrando queda devido à realização de lucros, após atingirem máximas de vários anos na semana passada, e a um recuo no preço do petróleo bruto, segundo os operadores.
Os futuros de soja apresentaram alta em alguns momentos em um pregão volátil, impulsionados pela alta acentuada dos futuros de farelo de soja em meio à escassez de oferta doméstica desse ingrediente para ração animal.
O contrato de soja novembro fechou em queda de 0,75 centavo, ou 0,06%, a US$13,1975 por bushel, permanecendo abaixo da máxima do contrato na semana passada, de US$13,3525.
O contrato de farelo de soja dezembro encerrou com alta de US$5,70, ou 1,6%, a US$371,30 por tonelada.
O contrato dezembro do milho recuou para US$5,305 o bushel, e o trigo caiu para US$7,27 o bushel.
(Reportagem de Julie Ingwersen)

items.body:
El Gobierno de Donald Trump permitirá que altos cargos iraníes asistan a la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas en Nueva York la próxima semana, informó el jueves el Departamento de Estado, a pesar de que Washington y Teherán siguen en guerra.
Un portavoz del Departamento de Estado dijo que se permitiría a una "delegación principal del régimen iraní" asistir a la reunión, en cumplimiento de las obligaciones de Estados Unidos como país anfitrión del organismo internacional.
Esto significa que se concederán visados a altos cargos como el presidente iraní, Masoud Pezeshkian, y el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, Abbas Araqchi, según una fuente familiarizada con la decisión.
La Administración del presidente Donald Trump ha mantenido conversaciones intermitentes con los líderes iraníes con el objetivo de poner fin a la guerra, que comenzó el 28 de febrero, cuando Estados Unidos e Israel atacaron Irán.
Teherán respondió con ataques contra Israel y los Estados del golfo Pérsico que albergan bases estadounidenses.
"La delegación estará sujeta a restricciones de viaje y se le prohibirá la compra de artículos de lujo y otros productos, de acuerdo con nuestra política. La delegación es más reducida que la del año pasado", añadió el portavoz del Departamento de Estado.
El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Irán no respondió de inmediato a la solicitud de comentarios de Reuters.

items.title: JPMorgan asset and wealth management operations head Julie Harris to retire in 2027
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Julie Harris, the global head of operations at JPMorgan Chase's asset and wealth management (AWM) arm, is set to retire in early 2027, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Thursday.
items.body:
Julie Harris, the global head of operations at JPMorgan Chase's (JPM.N) asset and wealth management (AWM) arm, is set to retire in early 2027, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Thursday.
Here are some more details:
Under Harris' leadership, the operations team played a vital role in helping JPMorgan's AWM business grow to more than $8 trillion in client assets under supervision from roughly $2 trillion.
"Julie has been one of the most influential leaders in AWM's transformation over the last decade. Since joining the firm in 2017, she has challenged us to rethink legacy ways of working, championed smarter and more scalable solutions," AWM CEO Mary Callahan Erdoes said in the memo.
Harris, who joined JPMorgan in 2017, also serves as the chief administrative officer of the AWM arm.
JPMorgan has chosen Fred Crosnier to lead AWM operations, starting January 1. He will report to Erdoes.
Crosnier began his career at JPMorgan in France and returned to the firm in 2019 after holding senior leadership roles across the financial services industry. Most recently, he was named deputy head of AWM operations.
JPMorgan plans to announce the successor for the asset management operations' lead role, which is currently held by Crosnier, in due course.

items.title: AI error-ridden court filings surge despite three years of court sanctions
items.author: Mike Scarcella
items.creator: Mike Scarcella
items.summary: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com)
items.body:
(Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com )
In a span of three days this month, a defense lawyer was rebuked for filing fabricated police witness testimony in a New Mexico murder case, prosecutors in Oklahoma disclosed that a judge's order there had cited fake cases, and a lawyer representing State Farm in Los Angeles was fined for erroneous citations across seven court filings.
The materials in each case were produced using generative AI, adding to a mountain of made-up, misquoted, misleading or incorrectly cited legal filings since the technology debuted on a mass scale in 2022.
Three years after the [USN:L1N38E2J1 TEXT:"first US court sanction"] over AI-generated errors, the number of attorneys admitting they used AI carelessly keeps growing, with AI errors now seeping into court opinions, expert testimony and prosecutors' briefs.
"You would have thought that the legal profession — armed with awareness that hallucinations can happen — would be more vigilant," said US District Judge P. Kevin Castel in Manhattan, whose 2023 order sanctioning lawyers for citing fake ChatGPT-generated cases became the profession's earliest warning.
Castel told Reuters that scrutiny from judges and the adversarial legal system meant AI errors were being exposed when they occur, and "that’s a wonderful thing.” But "as the problem continues without abatement, the need for sanctions that are a greater deterrent grows," he said.
AI "hallucinations" have now surfaced in at least 1,395 cases in US state and federal courts, according to a researcher tracking the cases on his website. Lawyers are generally not prohibited from using AI, but they are bound by ethics rules to verify the accuracy of their court submissions.
After a lawyer in New Mexico cited fabricated witnesses and made-up police testimony in his client's murder appeal, justices on the state's Supreme Court at a hearing last month [USN:L6N4521AB TEXT:"expressed exasperation"] that attorneys were still failing to vet their AI research.
“My 13-year-old nephew knows about hallucinations,” Justice C. Shannon Bacon had told the defense lawyer. “My 75-year-old stepmother knows about hallucinations.”
Bacon said the lawyer either chose not to understand the technology's limitations or "decided to roll the dice." The lawyer in that case [USN:L6N4521AB TEXT:"told Reuters"] he was remorseful and called the incident "a lesson learned for all professionals who rely upon this powerful but sometimes unstable technology."
Mark McKenna, co-director of the UCLA Institute of Technology, Law & Policy, blamed a mix of factors as contributing to the growing number of errors: a competitive rush among law firms to adopt AI, pressure to deliver work quickly and AI marketing that he said downplays risks.
“Lawyers keep making the judgment that the upside is better than the downside,” McKenna said.
The sanctions lawyers that have faced range from warnings and formal rebukes to monetary penalties in the hundreds to tens of thousands of dollars. Some judges have [USN:L2N3UY0WN TEXT:"referred lawyers"] to state bar authorities to consider their compliance with professional ethics rules.
In California last week, a lawyer representing State Farm was [USN:L6N456132 TEXT:"fined $999.99"] after generative AI produced a series of inaccurate citations and quotations.
"I accept full responsibility for my erroneous citations and make no excuses and express my deepest and sincerest apologies to the court," the lawyer had told the court.
State Farm in a statement this week said it “expects all external counsel to adhere to the highest standards of professionalism and ethical conduct, including when using AI and when reviewing and confirming the accuracy of all court filings.”
AI errors in judicial rulings have been rarer but have raised particular alarms. After hallucinated material was [USN:L6N44S0X9 TEXT:"included in decisions"] by two federal judges last year, US Senator Chuck Grassley of Iowa called on judges across the country to "formalize measures to prevent the misuse of artificial intelligence in their chambers."
In the Oklahoma case last week, a judge told a state investigator he had [USN:L6N451168 TEXT:"used an AI program for research"] and that an order he drafted contained two citations to non-existent cases.
A lawyer for the judge said they were declining to comment.
Also on Billable Hours' radar this week...
– Our legal industry columnist Sara Randazzo looks at [USN:L6N45215L TEXT:"what's driving the soaring pay for star recruits"], and how those investments might be leading firms to take risks they otherwise wouldn't have in the past.
– A senior Burford Capital executive and a former business partner have launched an AI-focused law firm for employment disputes and negotiations, [USN:L6N45719P TEXT:"joining a growing number"] of firms built around artificial intelligence.
– Also on the AI front: national plaintiffs firm Morgan & Morgan is [USN:L6N4560UK TEXT:"touting its planned $1 billion investment"] in AI and technology over the next decade and next year will begin marketing its own AI platform to other law firms.
– Conservative attorney John Eastman [USN:L6N43B13U TEXT:"asked the US Supreme Court"] to reinstate his California law license after his disbarment over his efforts helping Donald Trump contest his 2020 presidential election loss.
Read more:
[USN:L6N450049 TEXT:"Legal profession is ‘detrimental’ to mental health, say 41% of lawyers"]
[USN:L6N44S168 TEXT:"Rival lawyers clash over fees after $2.8 billion Blue Cross settlement"]
[USN:L6N44F19B TEXT:"Lawyers square off in fight over voice data used to train AI"]
[USN:L6N44411J TEXT:"US Supreme Court case tests fees for immigration detainees"]

items.title: Reuters launches Reuters Misinformation Monitor weekly newsletter to cut through false narratives and bring rigorous fact-checking expertise to global audiences
items.author: Reuters Communications
items.creator: Reuters Communications
items.summary: Reuters today announced the launch of Reuters Misinformation Monitor, a new weekly newsletter that delivers real-time intelligence on the global misinformation narratives shaping societies, global markets and policy.
items.body:
The Reuters Misinformation Monitor newsletter logo. Reuters today announced the launch of Reuters Misinformation Monitor, a new weekly newsletter that delivers real-time intelligence on the global misinformation narratives shaping societies, global markets and policy.
In an era when false claims can reshape public discourse, mislead markets and even impact policy decisions, Reuters is bringing its unmatched fact-checking infrastructure directly to readers. Led by Stephanie Burnett, Global Digital Verification Editor, Reuters Misinformation Monitor draws on fact-checking expertise from a team working in 17 languages to track false narratives as they emerge. Each week, the team will break down the week's most consequential false narratives, offering context and insight into how misinformation travels and influences outcomes.
"Reuters Misinformation Monitor brings our audience a snapshot of the false claims we're examining globally, providing a weekly rundown on what's happening so readers can stay ahead of the curve and make informed decisions,” said Burnett. "We're making accessible our expertise on the false narratives that mislead markets and influence decisions."
Each Wednesday, subscribers to Reuters Misinformation Monitor will receive a curated roundup of top global misinformation narratives examined by the Reuters verification team; "Real or Fake?" – an interactive quiz that tests readers' ability to spot false claims and doctored images; and direct access to Reuters fact checkers through reader submissions, allowing audiences to flag suspicious claims for investigation.
The international team behind Burnett and Reuters Misinformation Monitor includes:
Riniki Sanyal, the Fact-Checking Team Leader for Special Projects. Sanyal cut her teeth in the news industry by reporting on financial markets before becoming an editor and diving into the world of addressing misinformation. She joined Reuters in 2015.
Jennifer O’Mahony, a Fact-Checking Editor with 15 years of media experience, including as a West Africa correspondent, documentary producer, and a newspaper beat reporter. She joined Reuters in 2024.
Alejandra Ceballos, a Breaking News Correspondent based in Mexico City, where she examines Spanish and English -language online narratives that fan into the U.S. and Mexico. She previously worked as a researcher and a news coordinator before joining Reuters in 2022.
Lina Golovnya, a Fact-Checking Producer examining misinformation in Ukrainian, Russian and English — the bulk of which is focused on the Russia-Ukraine conflict. She joined Reuters in 2022 as a French markets reporter.
Subscribe to Reuters Misinformation Monitor here .
Media Contact:
Heather Carpenter
Heather.Carpenter @ tr.com

items.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル反落、原油安と金利低下で　焦点は日銀会合へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ニューヨーク　１７日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ニューヨーク　１７日　ロイター］ - 終盤のニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルがユーロに対して下落した。前日は米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が利上げに踏み切り、追加引き締めを示唆したことを受け、ユーロに対して３カ月ぶりの大幅な上昇を記録していた。

ユーロは０．１％高の１．１４７５５ドル。前日の１６日には、６月１７日以来最大となる０．７％の下落を記録していた。

主要６通貨に対するドルの強さを示すドル指数は、ほぼ横ばいの１００．２３となった。

１７日のドル下落は、前日の急騰からの反動に加え、米国債利回りの低下と原油価格の落ち着きが背景となった。

バノックバーン・フォレックスのチーフマーケットストラテジスト、マーク・チャンドラー氏は「ドルは足元で米金利と連動して動いていると思う」と指摘。前日の上昇後に米国債利回りが低下する中、「ドルはやや調整している」と述べた。

ＦＲＢは足元で市場のタカ派的な期待に応えた可能性があるものの、市場が想定するほど積極的に利上げしない可能性もあり、ドルは神経質な動きになっている。

市場はＦＲＢよりもはるかにタカ派的な見方を維持している。政策担当者が２０２６年にあと１回の利上げと２０２７年の据え置きを予想する一方、投資家は２０２６年に１回を超える追加利上げと、２０２７年末までに計約３回の利上げを織り込んでいる。

エネルギー価格の下落もドル安を促した。オマーン経由でのサウジアラビア産原油の追加供給が伝わり、供給懸念が和らいだためだ。

一方、英ポンドはユーロとドルに対して小幅安となった。イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）は政策金利を据え置いたものの、中東の紛争が長期化すれば引き締めが必要になる可能性があると警告した。英ポンドは終盤は０．２％安の１．３３５４ドルだった。

市場の関心は今、日銀に移っている。日銀は１８日に金利を３１年ぶりの高水準に引き上げると予想されている。ただ、ドルが底堅く推移する中、円相場の上値は限定されている。１７日はドル／円は０．２％安の１５６．０５５円となった。

ウェルズ・ファーゴのアジア太平洋地域マクロ戦略責任者、チドゥ・ナラヤナン氏は、日銀がすでに市場が織り込む積極的な引き締め路線を上回るタカ派姿勢を示せるかについて、懐疑的な見方を崩していない。「リスクは、市場の織り込みよりもハト派的な結果が出た場合に傾いている。そうした結果になれば、ドル／円が再び上昇する余地が生じるだろう」と述べた。

暗号資産（仮想通貨）のビットコインはほぼ変わらずの７万６５３５ドルとなった。

items.title: Colheita da safra principal de café da Colômbia está prestes a começar, com expectativas mais modestas
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Os cafeicultores colombianos, muitos dos quais ainda se recuperam dos danos causados pelo terremoto, estão prestes a iniciar a colheita da safra principal, com expectativas de produção estável e qualidade ligeiramente inferior, de acordo com a Sucafina, empresa especializada no comércio de commodities agrícolas.
items.body:
Os cafeicultores colombianos, muitos dos quais ainda se recuperam dos danos causados pelo terremoto, estão prestes a iniciar a colheita da safra principal, com expectativas de produção estável e qualidade ligeiramente inferior, de acordo com a Sucafina, empresa especializada no comércio de commodities agrícolas.
A empresa afirmou que o volume da nova safra (2026/27) deve ser semelhante ao da última temporada, que já havia sido menor.
A Sucafina não forneceu um número, mas o Departamento de Agricultura dos Estados Unidos projetou a safra anterior em 12,5 milhões de sacas de 60 kg e a nova safra (2026/27) em 13,4 milhões de sacas.
"Espera-se que a qualidade se mantenha em nível exportável, embora um pouco abaixo da safra principal anterior", disse a empresa, citando infestação de insetos em algumas áreas.
A empresa espera que volumes maiores cheguem ao mercado por volta de novembro e dezembro.
"Tivemos chuvas intensas ao longo do primeiro trimestre; depois, o padrão mudou para uma seca moderada durante o segundo e o terceiro trimestres. Esse tipo de oscilação não dá à safra muito espaço para se recuperar", disse Oscar Hurtado, diretor global de pesquisa de produção da Sucafina.
Segundo ele, o "verdadeiro teste" virá com a próxima Mitaca (colheita intermediária), quando o El Niño estiver em seu auge e influenciando diretamente as principais áreas de cultivo de café.
(Reportagem de Marcelo Teixeira)
